items.definition: To do a planned piece of work, such as a test, a survey or an order.
examples: The team carried out a survey of local shoppers.
Police are carrying out an investigation.

items.definition: To mention a subject for the first time in a conversation; also, to look after a child until adulthood.
examples: I didn't want to bring up money during dinner.
She was brought up by her grandparents.

items.definition: To say no to an offer, request or invitation; also, to lower the volume or heat of something.
examples: He turned down the job because the salary was too low.
Could you turn the music down? I'm trying to study.

items.definition: To find an answer by thinking or calculating; also, to end in a particular way, or to exercise.
examples: I can't work out how much we each owe.
Everything worked out well in the end.

items.definition: To deal with a problem successfully or to put things in order.
examples: The airline sorted out the mix-up with my booking.
I need to sort out my paperwork before the deadline.

items.definition: To examine the facts about a problem or situation in order to understand it.
examples: The manager promised to look into the complaint.
We are looking into cheaper energy suppliers.

items.definition: To get information about something, or to discover a fact that was not known before.
examples: I'll find out what time the museum closes.
She found out that her flight had been cancelled.

items.definition: To tell someone a fact that they have not noticed or have forgotten.
examples: She pointed out that the shop was already closed.
Let me point out one problem with this plan.

items.definition: To recover from an illness or a bad experience, or to deal with a difficulty.
examples: It took him weeks to get over the flu.
She still hasn't got over the shock of losing her job.

items.definition: To write the necessary information on a form; also, to give someone details they missed.
examples: Please fill in the form in capital letters.
Can you fill me in on what happened at the meeting?

items.definition: To leave an important job or position, usually of your own choice.
examples: The chairman will step down at the end of the year.
She stepped down as team captain after the final.
collocations: announce that you are stepping down

items.definition: To decide or say that something is impossible or will not be considered.
examples: Doctors have ruled out a serious infection.
The minister did not rule out raising taxes.

items.definition: To make something happen, especially a change.
examples: The internet has brought about huge changes in the way we shop.
Strong public pressure brought about a change in the law.

items.definition: To suggest an idea, plan or name for other people to consider.
examples: She put forward a proposal to open the library on Sundays.
Three candidates have been put forward for the post.
